note:
Measured on the assembled robot, 2026-09-07, dog inverted and unloaded.
centre: all 12 servos were driven to their own middle position (write 128 to TORQUE_ENABLE) while held at the model's mechanical zero, then --capture read the residual. This was necessary, not cosmetic: as assembled, six joints sat within 330 counts of the 0/4095 encoder wrap and could not reach their own soft limits (fr_knee needed +-1128 counts and had 16). Servo.to_counts clamps silently at 0/4095, so capturing there would have baked in joints that stop mid-command with nothing reporting it.
sign: --sign all, then re-verified by commanding all four legs of one axis at once and comparing them against each other. Three of the twelve --sign answers were wrong, all of them roll, all from the same cause -- the prompts are written in the robot's frame and the robot was belly-up, which reverses left and right (and swaps rear-left with rear-right). Pitch and knee were unaffected because their prompts ask about fore/aft, which the flip leaves alone. Verify roll with the robot the right way up, or with a comparison that never names a side.
The pattern is worth knowing before the next assembly: roll splits FRONT/REAR (+1,+1,-1,-1) while pitch and knee split LEFT/RIGHT (+1,-1,+1,-1).
